messages.content: My wife cannot get away early enough for either Friday flight we discussed. Please compare the last Friday departure with an early Saturday flight. The graduation and Monday return are unchanged, and we still need to be in Edina before Saturday dinner.

I found two nonstop choices for two travelers. Friday's last departure is Delta at 9:55 p.m., arriving Minneapolis at 11:33 p.m. The Saturday option departs at 7:10 a.m. and arrives at 8:48 a.m. Both use the unchanged Monday Delta return at 4:35 p.m., arriving Atlanta at 8:02 p.m. I'll price each with one king room at Graduate by Hilton Minneapolis.
Good. Include the full hotel totals, not just nightly rates, and keep the rideshare estimate in the comparison.

The late-Friday package is $1,074 for two Main Cabin tickets, $642 total for the king room from Friday through Monday, and about $120 for rideshares, for an estimated total of $1,836. You would reach the hotel shortly after midnight. The early-Saturday package is $884 for both tickets, $428 total for the same room from Saturday through Monday, and about $128 for rideshares, for an estimated total of $1,440. Saturday saves about $396.
Why are the rideshares slightly higher on Saturday?

The Saturday estimate includes an extra ride because the room is unlikely to be ready around 9:30 a.m. You could leave your bags at the hotel, go out, and return later to check in. The hotel confirms complimentary luggage storage. If you stay near campus after dropping the bags, the actual total may be closer to the Friday estimate.
And what time should we leave for the dinner from that hotel? Dinner starts at 6:30 in Edina.

I would request the ride at 5:35 p.m. That allows roughly 30 minutes in the car plus a buffer for Saturday traffic. Even with a moderate flight delay, the 8:48 a.m. arrival leaves substantial time before dinner.
The Saturday schedule makes more sense. Before you book, confirm the fare rules and the hotel cancellation deadline.

The $884 airfare is Delta Main Cabin for two. Changes are permitted without a change fee, but any fare difference would apply; the tickets are not refundable to the original payment method. The Graduate king room is $428 including taxes and mandatory fees. It can be canceled without charge through 11:59 p.m. local hotel time on Wednesday, May 13. After that, the hotel charges one night's room and tax.
Does the room cover both of us, and is the Saturday arrival noted even though check-in will be later?

Yes. It is one king room for two adults for Saturday, May 16 through Monday, May 18. The reservation can note an expected morning bag drop and a later formal check-in. The hotel will hold the room through the night, so going directly to dinner after an afternoon check-in would not be a problem.
All right. Book the Saturday nonstop and the Monday return for both of us, then reserve that one king room. No insurance or other add-ons.

Please confirm authorization to charge $884 for the two Delta tickets and $428 for the hotel reservation, for $1,312 charged or secured now. Estimated rideshares of $128 are separate, making the expected trip total $1,440.

Both reservations are confirmed. Delta confirmation R6K2VP covers two Main Cabin passengers on the nonstop Atlanta-Minneapolis flight Saturday, May 16, departing 7:10 a.m. and arriving 8:48 a.m., and the nonstop return Monday, May 18, departing 4:35 p.m. and arriving Atlanta at 8:02 p.m. The airfare charged is $884. Graduate by Hilton Minneapolis confirmation GH-730184 is for one king room for two adults, May 16-18, at $428 including taxes and mandatory fees. Complimentary morning luggage storage and later check-in are noted. Cancellation is free through 11:59 p.m. Minneapolis time on May 13; after that, one night's room and tax applies. No insurance or optional extras were added. With estimated rideshares, the expected trip total is $1,440.
